headline: Dozens wounded as Houthi missile hits Riyadh airport
summary: Witnesses report panic and evacuations at the Saudi capital's international airport following an alleged missile strike.
details: Yemen's Houthi rebels allegedly attacked Riyadh's international airport with a missile on Saturday afternoon, leaving dozens of people wounded and causing widespread panic in the terminal.
A witness at the domestic terminal reported seeing a strike hit gate 401, while a local hospital source stated that five people are in intensive care and dozens more were injured overall.
Three witnesses confirmed that passengers were evacuated from the airport, and the airport's official X account urged travelers to check their flight status before heading to the facility.
The attack comes after a similar Houthi-claimed strike on Thursday that killed three people, including a pilot, and damaged a grounded Saudia plane.
Saudi authorities have not officially confirmed the latest attack or the evacuations, though they have rarely issued public statements regarding Houthi strikes on civilian targets recently.
The Houthis have repeatedly targeted Saudi airports and oil facilities since a truce in their long-running war with the Riyadh-backed Yemeni government collapsed in July.
Meanwhile, Saudi-supported government forces are reportedly advancing against the Houthis in Yemen, particularly around the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait.
caption:
Dozens injured and panic erupts at Riyadh airport after an alleged Houthi missile strike.

Yemen's Houthi rebels allegedly attacked Riyadh's international airport with a missile on Saturday afternoon, leaving dozens of people wounded and causing widespread panic in the terminal.

A witness at the domestic terminal reported seeing a strike hit gate 401, while a local hospital source stated that five people are in intensive care and dozens more were injured overall.

Three witnesses confirmed that passengers were evacuated from the airport, and the airport's official X account urged travelers to check their flight status before heading to the facility.

The attack comes after a similar Houthi-claimed strike on Thursday that killed three people, including a pilot, and damaged a grounded Saudia plane.

Saudi authorities have not officially confirmed the latest attack or the evacuations, though they have rarely issued public statements regarding Houthi strikes on civilian targets recently.

The Houthis have repeatedly targeted Saudi airports and oil facilities since a truce in their long-running war with the Riyadh-backed Yemeni government collapsed in July.

Meanwhile, Saudi-supported government forces are reportedly advancing against the Houthis in Yemen, particularly around the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait.

headline_marked: Biman [[suspends Dhaka-Riyadh flights]] until further notice
headline: Biman suspends Dhaka-Riyadh flights until further notice
summary: The national flag carrier halted services due to a suspension of inbound flights at King Khalid International Airport in Saudi Arabia.
details: Biman Bangladesh Airlines has suspended its Dhaka-Riyadh-Dhaka flights BG339 and BG340 until further notice.
The decision follows a suspension of all inbound flights at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
Passengers booked on the affected flights have been advised not to travel to the airport.
Biman is currently assessing the situation and will provide an update on the status or rescheduling of flights tomorrow, October 11.
Affected passengers are urged to contact Biman's call centre or visit the nearest sales office for further assistance.
caption:
Flight suspension alert! Biman halts all Dhaka-Riyadh services due to airport closures in Saudi Arabia.

Biman Bangladesh Airlines has suspended its Dhaka-Riyadh-Dhaka flights BG339 and BG340 until further notice.

The decision follows a suspension of all inbound flights at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

Passengers booked on the affected flights have been advised not to travel to the airport.

Biman is currently assessing the situation and will provide an update on the status or rescheduling of flights tomorrow, October 11.

Affected passengers are urged to contact Biman's call centre or visit the nearest sales office for further assistance.
